title: French Bulldog Hemivertebrae and Screw Tail: Spine Problems
seoTitle: French Bulldog Hemivertebrae and Screw Tail
description: French Bulldog hemivertebrae explained: why the screw tail and spine are linked, how common it is, which symptoms matter, X-ray vs MRI, and treatment.

faq.a: No. French Bulldogs are born with a naturally short tail, straight or screwed. The screw tail is linked to a DVL2 gene variant that all French Bulldogs carry.

faq.q: Do all French Bulldogs have hemivertebrae?
faq.a: Not all, but most. In a CT study, 93.5% of French Bulldogs without neurological signs had at least one hemivertebra, and most never showed symptoms from it.

faq.q: What are the symptoms of hemivertebrae in French Bulldogs?
faq.a: When a malformation presses on the spinal cord, the typical sign is back-leg weakness and wobbliness that worsens over time, usually starting in young dogs. Sudden paralysis is an emergency and is more often caused by a disc problem.

faq.q: Can hemivertebrae be seen on an X-ray?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Most vertebral malformations are visible on X-rays, but CT and MRI are needed to judge whether the spinal cord is compressed and whether surgery could help.

faq.q: Does my French Bulldog need surgery for hemivertebrae?
faq.a: Only if the malformation is causing neurological signs. For dogs with progressive weakness, the Royal Veterinary College reports better results with surgical stabilization than with medical treatment alone.
